title: Deployment Exposure Bridge and Rollback Collage
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact visual layer — the 'Exposure Bridge' — that connects traffic split configuration to the rollback timeline and decision surface. The feature combines a contextual timeline, live metrics preview, and a compact rollback 'collage' of automated and manual policies to help engineers and PMs reason about progressive exposure and fast recovery.
background: Current rollout views surface traffic splits and separate rollback controls as separate panels. Field teams report friction in correlating a traffic change to time-series signals and identifying which rollback policy will fire. This reduces confidence during fast canaries and increases time-to-revert for incidents.
goals: Surface a single horizontally-scoped exposure timeline that shows percentage ramps, cohorts, and metric anchors
Allow inline hypothesis annotations (why this ramp exists, owners, expected metrics)
Expose primary rollback triggers and preview what an automatic rollback would do (which variant, how much traffic would shift)
Make it possible to simulate a quick rollback or partial revert from the same surface with one click
Keep the UI keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly for on-call workflows
acceptance_criteria: Exposure Bridge appears as a horizontal band above the rollout editor and shows time-aligned traffic percentages and metric sparklines
Clicking a segment reveals hypothesis metadata and the rollback policy card for that segment
Automatic rollback cards display trigger thresholds, affected variants, and a simulated traffic reflow preview
Users can trigger a staged rollback (50% -> 0%) or full rollback directly from the collage, with confirmation modal that lists dependent routes
Feature passes keyboard navigation tests and basic screen reader readouts for key elements
decisions: Keep exposure timeline read-only in the initial release; edits must be done in the editor below to reduce accidental changes
Show two layers of metrics: fast-sampling sparkline (latency/errors) and one selectable KPI chart for deeper inspection
Automatic rollback preview will show only compatible fallback variants (same model family or pinned compatibility tags)
Rollbacks initiated from collage will trigger the same rollout events as the existing rollback API to maintain event consistency
tradeoffs: Embedding simulation in the UI increases perceived complexity — mitigated by progressive disclosure and a learn-more tooltip
Keeping timeline read-only reduces direct in-context editing but prevents accidental drift during on-call operations
Showing multiple KPIs clutters the bridge; we default to two (latency + error rate) and make others opt-in
open_questions: Should rollback previews include cost delta estimates for reverting to smaller models or quantized variants?
How to represent cross-route dependencies when a rollback affects upstream routing?
Do we allow team-level defaults for which KPI is shown in the bridge, or should it be per-rollout?
implementation_notes: Frontend: new ExposureBridge React component; timeline uses existing timeline-token library for consistent anchoring
Backend: add /rollouts/:id/preview-rollback endpoint that reuses rollout engine simulation to return traffic reflow and affected variants
Telemetry: emit exposure_interaction events (open_segment, preview_rollback, trigger_rollback) for audit and usability analysis
A11y: ensure clickable cards have aria-expanded and provide alt text for mini-sparklines
